statement: The opening argument proves that a general cubic surface contains exactly 27 lines, using five tritangent planes through each line; the next paragraph gives an argument not assuming a line beforehand.

source.version: 1889 Collected Mathematical Papers, vol.I, no.76, pp.445–456, reprinting Cambridge and Dublin Mathematical Journal 4(1849),118–132; RCIN scan

scope: Lines on a general smooth complex cubic surface in projective three-space.
notes:
The original author explicitly credits Salmon for determining the number. The 1849 identity and 1889 result locator are both retained.

Originality audit: Salmon is credited by Cayley for determining the number 27; Cayley supplies the argument described in this record. Both historical contributions are retained. Salmon’s original text has not been inspected here.
